extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and advanced students concerned with the foundations and logical justification of Newtonian fluxions / infinitesimal calculus
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the legitimacy, logical form, and conceptual grounding of demonstrations and methods in the fluxionary (Newtonian) calculus — in particular whether infinitesimals/evanescent increments and the manipulations of them are justified, consistent, and scientifically clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles must prove conclusions (not vice versa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Men prove their Conclusions by their Principles, and not their Principles by the Conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legitimate demonstration must proceed from stated premises to derived conclusions. One must not infer or establish foundational principles by appealing to conclusions that presuppose them; reversing this order is 'contrary to the Rules of Logic' and amounts to induction or mere presumption rather than demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the method, not merely the truth of theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: I am not concerned about the truth of your Theorems, but only about the way of coming at them; whether it be legitimate or illegitimate, clear or obscure, scientific or tentative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging mathematical work, focus on the legitimacy, clarity, and scientific status of the method used to obtain results rather than only on whether the final results happen to be correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in premises propagate to conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever errors are admitted in the Premises, proportional errors ought to be apprehended in the Conclusion, be they finite or infinitesimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that small or infinitesimal errors in premises have no effect; logically a real error in premises produces a corresponding (possibly proportional) real error in conclusions unless explicitly justified otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting infinitesimal terms requires justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rule for this is got by rejecting the Product or Rectangle of the Differences... it is supposed that no Quantity is bigger or lesser for the Addition or Subduction of its Infinitesimal, and that consequently no error can arise from such rejection of Infinitesimals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discarding higher-order (product) infinitesimal terms is not automatically legitimate; the analyst must justify why such rejections do not produce unaccounted errors (e.g., by algebraic cancellation or other valid reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of errors does not equal valid demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: By virtue of a twofold mistake you arrive, though not at Science, yet at Truth... Error may bring forth Truth, though it cannot bring forth Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arriving at a correct result because two distinct errors cancel is insufficient: the method remains illegitimate and unscientific. A proper demonstration must show why the result holds, not rely on fortuitous error cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistent suppositions (finite then vanishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is supposed that the Abscissas a and b are unequal, without which no one step could have been made; and in the second place, it is supposed they are equal; which is a manifest Inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make steps that require a quantity to be both finite (to carry out certain constructions) and at the same time treated as zero/vanishing; such inconsistent switching invalidates the logical chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate limit-objects with limiting relations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Secant cannot be a Tangent, so a Subsecant cannot be a Subtangent... the Subsecant will always be less than the Subtangent, and can never coincide with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear distinction between a limiting object (tangent) and the approximating objects (secants/subsecants). You cannot legitimately treat a secant as if it were the tangent in constructions unless a valid limiting argument is provided that preserves logical consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences dependent on an increment must be removed if the increment is set to zero
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not legitimate or logical to suppose 0 to vanish, i.e. to be nothing, i.e. that there is no Increment, unless we reject at the same time with the Increment itself every consequence of such Increment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you set an increment to zero in an equation or argument, you must also eliminate all terms and consequences that depended on that increment, or otherwise provide an algebraic justification (e.g., cancellation by equals) for maintaining particular derived terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of quantities must be justified by algebraic cancellation or equals-on-both-sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Because qg being Unite, go is equal to o: And therefore 2x + 0o — go = y = 2x... the true reason hereof is plainly this: Because the equal Quantities 90 and o being destroyed by contrary Signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throwing away terms is legitimate only if they are annihilated by equal opposite terms (i.e., subtracting equals from equals) or otherwise shown algebraically to vanish; mere appeal to 'infinitesimal smallness' is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using consequences of a hypothesis after the hypothesis has been abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: It is sophistical to suppose NO or RP, PS, and SR to be finite real Lines in order to form the Triangle RPS... and afterwards to suppose there are no such Lines, nor consequently similar Triangles, and nevertheless to retain the Consequence of the first Supposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you derive consequences under a temporary hypothesis, you cannot later discard the hypothesis while still using those consequences — that is logically invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical methods practiced without knowledge of their principles are not scientific demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Rules may be practiced by Men who neither attend to, nor perhaps know the Principles... you may operate and compute and solve Problems thereby, not only without an actual Attention to, or an actual Knowledge of, the Grounds of that Method... yet you may not be justly esteemed a Man of Science and Demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical competence in using rules does not substitute for understanding foundational principles; scientific status requires clarity about the grounds and legitimacy of the method used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols alone are not sufficient; concepts must be intelligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Men too often impose on themselves and others, as if they conceived and understood things expressed by Signs, when in truth they have no Idea, save only of the very Signs themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on symbolic manipulation without clear conceptual understanding of what the symbols represent (e.g., velocities, fluxions); symbolic facility must be matched by intelligible definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluxions/velocities must be grounded in measurable notions (time and space)
rubrics_metrics.description: How can we conceive a Velocity by it introduced? Is it not to shun or, rather to palliate the Use of Quantities infinitely small? But we have no Notion whereby to conceive and measure various Degree of Velocity, beside Space and Time, of alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of fluxions as 'velocities' require a clear reference to time and space (or other measurable bases). Avoid defining velocities or fluxions abstractly without indicating how they are to be measured or compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: If finite proxies for fluxions are used, the steps to obtain them must themselves be clear
rubrics_metrics.description: If fluxions may be expounded or expressed by finite Lines proportional to them: Which finite Lines, as they may be distinctly conceived and known and reasoned upon, so they may be substituted for the Fluxions... if, in order to arrive at these finite Lines proportional to the Fluxions, there be certain Steps made use of which are obscure and inconceivable, ... your proceeding is not clear nor your method scientific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to replace fluxions by finite proportional quantities only if the derivation of those finite proxies is itself done by clear, legitimate, and comprehensible steps; otherwise the substitution conceals lack of rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: A correct conclusion obtained by dubious steps is not a valid demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Conclusion is evident and the Premises obscure, or the Conclusion accurate and the Premises inaccurate, we may safely pronounce that such Conclusion is neither evident nor accurate, in virtue of those obscure or inaccurate Premises or Principles; but in virtue of some other Principles which perhaps the Demonstrator himself never knew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theorem whose truth relies on hidden or unknown principles is not properly demonstrated. Demonstrations should make explicit the principles that lend legitimacy to the conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit/ultimate-ratio arguments must not invoke impossibilities (e.g., triangles 'in a point')
rubrics_metrics.description: It is particularly remarked ... that the Points C and c must not be distant one from another, by any the least Interval whatsoever: But that, in order to find the ultimate Proportions ... the Point C and c must be accurately coincident, i.e. one and the same. A Point therefore is considered as a Triangle, or a Triangle is supposed to be formed in a Point. Which is a direct Fallacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of metaphysical or logically impossible images used to justify limit arguments (e.g., forming a triangle in a point); limits must be treated by legitimate limiting procedures, not by imagining impossible coincidences.

rubrics_metrics.name: The doctrine of fluxions must work equally in finite and infinitesimal contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: This hint may, perhaps, be further extended and applied to good purpose... The use I make of it is to show, that the Analysis cannot obtain in Augments or Tiny [only], but it must also obtain in finite Quantities, be they ever so great.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sound foundation should demonstrate that the analytic/fluxionary relationships are coherent both when increments are treated as infinitesimal and when treated as finite; the method should not rely exclusively on appealing to 'evanescent' notions without finite analogues.
